supersedes: an earlier 'skip S3' decision that was based on Switched_Filter's share alone
why_the_earlier_decision_was_wrong: Only Switched_Filter's share was reported (35.3% -> 20.6% -> 9.1%) and read as flattening.
Uniform over six classes is 16.7%, so 9.1% is BELOW chance: the mass did not spread, it moved.
Under the normalized +-1 scorer Switched_Line absorbs it and reaches 49.7%.
Total variation from uniform gets WORSE under normalization: 0.349 -> 0.461.
correction_to_s0_finding: The +8 bonus WAS the driver of Switched_Filter's specific dominance -- that part of the +8 experiment stands. But removing it did not balance the pool; it relocated the peak. The heuristic scorer is degenerate under both magnitude schemes, which strengthens the case for retiring it as a label source (S0) and removes any basis for skipping S3.
what_s3_requires: Margin stratification m(s) = r*_(1) - r*_(2) over the eval pool, binned easy/medium/boundary, computed per switch_model, with selector accuracy reported per stratum alongside the existing area_rank and frequency-band axes. A pool where one class holds ~50% lets a constant predictor score ~50%, so aggregate accuracy is not interpretable without it.
blocked_on: r_star (tools/compute_envelope.py). m(s) is defined in terms of the top-two envelope values.
